speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; please tell me, what specific conditions are included in your medical history?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing those symptoms. You mentioned feeling clumsy specifically on the right side; does this ataxia worsen when you walk in the dark, and have you noticed any changes in your speech or vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) induced by natalizumab therapy.

The combination of recent onset gait and limb ataxia, specifically worsening on the right side, alongside a history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab (a potent immunosuppressant known to carry this risk), strongly suggests Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). To confirm this, I need to see your brain imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with contrast. Additionally, I need to review the results of your recent Lumbar_Puncture to check for JC_Virus DNA.
